mechanism: Both drugs have anticholinergic properties; dutasteride has mild anticholinergic effects while oxybutynin is a potent anticholinergic, leading to additive anticholinergic effects and potential urinary retention paradox in BPH patients.
action: Monitor for enhanced anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, cognitive impairment, urinary retention); consider alternative antimuscarinic with less anticholinergic burden or dose adjustment; counsel patient on fluid intake and bowel regimen.
